task.description: Idiom/scope gate on REQ-245 (chunk 238b1 of the REQ-238 split, ISS-0424 part 3b-1, queue task 483): applying REQ-237's .zig provenance-marking convention to lib/letflow/engine.ex and lib/letflow/engine/{execution_error,expr,instance_state,join_counter,pin_rebind,pin_resolver,plugin_interface,plugin_registry}.ex. Branch feature/WF02-REQ245-20260905, commit e67cd689, off main@44c12fe2.

result.summary: Independently re-verified all of ELIXIR-DEV's claims by direct grep/diff against main and the branch, not by trusting the handoff's summary. Findings: (1) Pre-existing marker count is 0 in all 9 files on main (re-derived via `git show main:<file> | grep -c`). (2) Post-change marker counts re-derived independently: engine.ex=1, execution_error.ex=1, expr.ex=7, instance_state.ex=2, join_counter.ex=1, pin_rebind.ex=1, pin_resolver.ex=5, plugin_interface.ex=1, plugin_registry.ex=1, total=20 -- matches the handoff's claimed total of 20 exactly. Note: the handoff's own per-file 'marker_lines_inserted_after' table misreports expr.ex as 6 (it is 7 -- 6 heredoc markers plus 1 '# '-prefixed comment marker); this is a bookkeeping slip in the handoff's table, not a real discrepancy -- git diff --stat independently shows expr.ex at 7 insertions, matching my grep, and the reported grand total (20) was already correct. Flagging as a documentation-accuracy note, not a rework blocker. (3) .zig line count identical before/after in all 9 files (2/3/8/2/2/2/7/1/1) -- re-derived independently via `git show main:<file> | grep -c '\.zig'` vs. `grep -c '\.zig'` on the branch, zero citations lost. (4) An independent awk scan (blank line resets 'marked' state, PROVENANCE line sets it, any .zig line un-preceded by a marker within its block flags UNMARKED) run against all 9 files found zero residuals. (5) git diff --stat against main confirms only the 9 in-scope lib/ files changed (9 files, 20 insertions, 0 deletions -- pure additive diff), plus expected handoff/registry bookkeeping files outside lib/. No sibling-chunk file (token.ex, transition.ex, routers/*, etc.) touched. (6) Read every one of the 9 files' full diffs end to end: every hunk is a single `+PROVENANCE (historical, not current decision authority):` line insertion immediately above a citation unit; zero existing line's text was altered anywhere.

judgment_calls_resolved.question: expr.ex's Rules 2/3 comment (transition.zig:1177/:1183, inside a `cond do` true-branch, a bare Elixir `#` comment block, not a heredoc/string) got a '# '-prefixed marker instead of a bare marker line. Does this break single-regex greppability (AC-2), and does the same reasoning REQ-243's REVIEWER already blessed for this adaptation apply here?
judgment_calls_resolved.verdict: Yes, same reasoning applies, no rework needed. Read the actual context directly (lib/letflow/engine/expr.ex:215-232): the marker sits inside `true -> # PROVENANCE (historical...)` immediately above the existing `# Rules 2/3: ...transition.zig:1177/:1183...` comment block, same shape as the bare-#-comment cases REQ-243's REVIEWER already tested and blessed (audit.ex, definitions.ex, identity.ex, instances.ex). Independently re-tested `grep -c`, `grep -Ec`, and `grep -Fc` against the literal marker text on expr.ex -- all three return 7, matching the bare-line marker count exactly; the '# ' prefix does not break substring greppability. This is the same syntactic-necessity adaptation for a context (bare Elixir source comment outside any heredoc/string) that design section 2 never enumerates, and the design's own verification command in section 5 is a plain substring match with no line-start anchor. No design gap, no rework.

judgment_calls_resolved.question: expr.ex's 'Sentinel result...' @typedoc and pin_resolver.ex's moduledoc/@typedoc heredocs contain multiple blank-line-separated citation sub-paragraphs, each treated as its own marker unit rather than one marker per heredoc. Is this the correct reading of design section 2's unit definition, and was any residual unmarked citation missed?
judgment_calls_resolved.verdict: Correct reading, confirmed by direct inspection, no residual missed. Design section 2 defines the paragraph unit as 'the whole paragraph (bounded by blank lines)' with no exception or aggregation rule for paragraphs sharing one heredoc/string literal -- a heredoc is not itself a unit, it is a container that can hold multiple blank-line-bounded paragraphs, each independently a unit under the same rule that applies to plain Markdown prose. Read expr.ex:104-122 directly: the @typedoc's first sub-paragraph (Sentinel result..., ends at line 110) and second sub-paragraph (REVIEWER GATE OQ-1 RESOLVED..., starts line 113) are separated by a genuine blank line (114), and both independently cite evaluator.zig -- both correctly carry their own marker. Read pin_resolver.ex:113-152 directly: the OQ-1 first sub-paragraph (marked, ends ~133, cites pin_resolver.zig multiple times) is separated by a blank line (134) from the second sub-paragraph ('Both deltas...', starts 135) which was deliberately left unmarked -- verified by reading it in full that it cites only ISS-0079.yaml/iss-0079-pin-override-verification.md/ISS-0078.yaml/iss-0078-pin-rebind-provenance.md, zero .zig substring, so leaving it unmarked is correct, not a miss. The independent awk residual scan (finding 4 above) confirms zero unmarked .zig lines remain anywhere in any of the 9 files.

judgment_calls_resolved.question: Are the two deliberate-divergence lines (execution_error.ex, pin_resolver.ex -- 'unlike R-Co' phrasing) byte-identical to main, only shifted by line number?
judgment_calls_resolved.verdict: Confirmed byte-identical, shifted exactly as claimed. execution_error.ex: main line 7 vs. branch line 8 (+1, matching the single marker inserted earlier in the same moduledoc) -- `diff` on the extracted lines shows zero difference. pin_resolver.ex: main line 141 vs. branch line 145 (+4, matching the 4 markers inserted earlier in the same file before this line) -- `diff` on the extracted lines shows zero difference. Also ran an unconstrained `grep -rnE 'unlike R-Co|deliberately diverges|diverges from R-Co'` across all 9 files with no line-list assumption: found exactly these two lines and no others, confirming no third divergence line was missed or altered.

result.documentation_follow_up_note: Same as REQ-243's REVIEWER flagged: worth a design-doc completeness amendment to req237-zig-provenance-marking-convention.md section 2 or 3 to explicitly enumerate (a) the bare-#-Elixir-comment context and its '# '-prefix adaptation, and (b) that a heredoc/string literal containing multiple blank-line-separated citation paragraphs gets one marker per paragraph, not one marker per heredoc -- both are now independently re-derived twice (REQ-243 and REQ-245) from the same section-2 paragraph-unit rule without needing rework, so the reading is stable, but a future chunk (244/246-253) would benefit from not having to re-derive it a third time. This is a documentation-completeness note, not a rework blocker on this diff.
